# Exact all-normal interface for the R4 product calibration

SUPERSEDED: the finite exact certificate is now complete, with root and
Two-sided full audits. See
`candidate de93c4f08837e128`
and `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`. The text below records the
original interface, rather than the current proof status.

This note specifies an UNPROVED finite inequality. It records no depth
certificate and must not be cited as actual global criticality.

Let P={z in Z^2:min(-z1-z2,2z1-z2,2z2-z1)>=-4}, so |P|=31,
and let K be a triangle with centroid g. The proposed canonical caps
have raw mass(40/3)|K|, all section centroids(0,g), and normalized
mass40/93. A separate exact martingale certificate bounds the complete
normal-dependent convex-potential efficiency of that profile by40/93.
Its standalone verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_r4_facet_martingale_slab_recovery.py`. This profile statement
does not prove those caps globally minimize mass at(0,g).

The independent vertex-permutation groups of the base triangle and K
preserve the actual mixed measure. Averaging the orbit of ANY point
in S gives(0,g), and the depth superlevel sets are convex. Hence(0,g)
is an actual global deepest point. This does not determine its depth.

Every normal with a nonzero continuous component can be reduced by
these independent permutations and positive scaling as follows. Its
ordered centered continuous vertex values are(1,c,-1-c), with
-1/2<=c<=1. The ordered values at the PRIMITIVE base vertices
e1,e2,(-1,-1) are(a,b,-a-b), with
a>=0 and -a/2<=b<=a. Thus the base value at z is L=az1+bz2.
For distinct continuous values, the total fraction of fiber volumes
captured by the through-(0,g) halfspace is

 [(1+2c) sum_z(L+1)_+^2
  -(2+c) sum_z(L+c)_+^2
  +(1-c) sum_z(L-1-c)_+^2]
 /[(1-c)(2+c)(1+2c)].                              (1)

This is the elementary triangle divided-difference cap formula summed
over the ACTUAL31 bases. At repeated continuous values, use its true
continuous limit; the cut planes have zero area in each fiber.

The missing lower bound is that(1)>=40/3 for all of these parameters.
Exploratory differential evolution on a<=1,4,20,100 found minima
13.6846559767,40/3,40/3,40/3 respectively; THIS IS NOT A PROOF.
No smaller-cap witness was found. The equality patterns were the
canonical ordered directions c=-1/2,b=-a/2 with sufficiently large a.

There is a compact exact alternative parameterization. Normalize the
maximum positive PRIMITIVE base vertex value plus the maximum positive
continuous vertex value to1. Equivalently, one quarter of the maximum
value at a D4 vertex plus the maximum continuous vertex value equals1.
Use

 0<=a<=1,  -a/2<=b<=a,  -(1-a)/2<=c<=1-a,
 L=az1+bz2,  (h0,h1,h2)=(1-a,c,-1+a-c).

The parameter domain is the tetrahedron with vertices
(0,0,-1/2),(0,0,1),(1,-1/2,0),(1,1,0).
The93 quantities L+h_j are affine. Their hyperplanes partition this
compact tetrahedron into finitely many rational polytopes. On each
sign cell, after clearing the positive denominator
D=(h0-h1)(h0-h2)(h1-h2), the desired inequality is the cubic

 (h1-h2) sum_z(L+h0)_+^2
 -(h0-h2) sum_z(L+h1)_+^2
 +(h0-h1) sum_z(L+h2)_+^2 -(40/3)D >=0.             (2)

Within a fixed sign cell every positive part in(2) is either its
displayed affine square or zero. An exhaustive rational cell subdivision
and nonnegative degree3 Bernstein certificate would prove(2), if one
can be completed. None has been completed here. Repeated continuous
values follow by continuity. Pure-base normals lie on a=1; their closed
halfspaces can be treated directly or by outward threshold shifts and
continuity of the original finite fiber measure, never by silently
discarding their boundary-fiber mass. More directly, perturb a nonzero
pure-base normal by continuous normals tending to zero. Pointwise the
limsup of the perturbed closed-cap indicators is at most the indicator
of the limiting CLOSED pure-base cap. Reverse Fatou for this finite
measure gives limiting cap mass at least the limsup of the perturbed
masses. Thus a lower bound already proved for all nonzero continuous
normals transfers to every pure-base closed halfspace without dropping
any of its boundary fibers.

The strict proper-minor COUNT quotas for this base are being separately
proved by Slab. Even if both the quota and lower-bound certificates
finish, this example would obstruct only another proposed auxiliary
individual-efficiency theorem. Its depth is far above the OC target.
